title: Office of Undergraduate Research (WashU)
description:
WashU's central hub for undergraduate research across all disciplines, coordinating funding, mentorship matching, and dissemination. OUR runs the internal award programs (AYURA, SURGE, Conference Travel Award), the WashU Research Ambassador Program, and the undergraduate research symposia. Contact: undergradresearch@wustl.edu.

title: Academic Year Undergraduate Research Award — AYURA (WashU)
compensation_details: Up to $2,500 in project expenses
description: A budget-based award of up to $2,500 supporting project expenses for student-initiated, faculty-mentored independent research or creative work in the Humanities, Social Sciences, and Arts. Originally term-time only, AYURA is now also available in summer to help rising seniors launch thesis research. Requires a faculty mentor and a project budget.

title: SURGE — Summer Undergraduate Research Guided Experience (WashU)
description: A summer program providing stipends and flexible programming for WashU undergraduates pursuing faculty-mentored, project-based inquiry across all academic disciplines. Strong candidates develop a research proposal, secure a nomination from their faculty research mentor, and immerse themselves in the WashU undergraduate research community over the summer.

title: Conference Travel Award (WashU Office of Undergraduate Research)
compensation_details: Up to $500 in conference travel support
description: Financial support of up to $500 for WashU undergraduates to present faculty-mentored research at professional academic conferences. Students must be nominated by a WashU faculty mentor; priority goes to students who have not previously used the award.

title: WashU Research Ambassador Program (WRAP)
description: A peer-mentoring program in which trained undergraduate Research Ambassadors serve as the student face of the Office of Undergraduate Research, increasing awareness of and access to undergraduate research across disciplines. title: Pulitzer Center Reporting Fellowship (WashU)
description: A competitive fellowship, administered through the Office of Undergraduate Research, funding a WashU undergraduate to pursue an underreported global issue as a reporting project in partnership with the Pulitzer Center.
